title: The Dancing Paper Stars
markdown:
In Mr. Kellan’s warm workshop, sunlight spilled like honey. Little paper stars, smaller than ladybugs, danced from the workbench and floated toward a rosy-red balloon tied to a high shelf.

Hazel’s eyes went wide. “Fizz, do you see that?”

Fizz the ferret, who had been chasing his tail, stopped and tilted his head. The stars drifted, then clung softly to the balloon.

“They seem to like it,” he rumbled.

Hazel giggled. “How?” She tried a feather; they floated just out of reach. Fizz nudged one with his nose; too light. A peaceful puzzle.

Kellan, humming, noticed. “They’ve found a friend who can pull them closer with an invisible thread.”

He rubbed a soft woolly sock on his tweed trousers and brought it near a cluster that had drifted from the balloon. The stars gathered and stuck, a cozy harbor.

“They’re sticking! How?”

He sat, eyes twinkling, and named it once: static electricity. Rubbing made a gentle force; very light things wanted to join. Same reason they liked the balloon. Invisible attraction.

“The balloon had that energy too?”

“Indeed. Rub your socks on the rug. You’ll attract them as well.”

They hurried, colourful socks on the cozy rug, then brought the charged pairs near the remaining stars. Softly the stars drifted on, clustering. Soon all were gathered.

“A science game,” Fizz wiggled.

Kellan smiled and did not mention clouds gathering or send them into dreams of quiet wonders. Useful, yes. All around, even unseen. He left it there.

Afternoon mellowed. They sat with their collected stars, then boxed them in a little wooden tin so the balloon could not start a second dance without asking. The first evening stars showed in the windows. Hazel peeled off her socks. Fizz, for once, did not chase his tail; he watched the tin, as if the paper might still be thinking about the balloon.
